subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The ionisation energy of an atom is the energy needed to:
options: Excite an electron to the next level
Completely remove an electron from the atom in its ground state
questions.explain: Ionisation energy is the energy required to remove an electron entirely (to the n = ∞, zero-energy level) from a ground-state atom.

questions.q: The photoelectric effect demonstrates that light is:
options: Quantised into discrete packets of energy called photons
questions.explain: The instantaneous, frequency-dependent emission shows light delivers energy in discrete quanta (photons), demonstrating quantisation.

questions.q: Why does photoelectric emission occur almost instantaneously when light above the threshold frequency strikes a metal?
options: A single photon delivers all its energy to one electron at once
questions.explain: A photon transfers its energy to a single electron in one interaction, so emission is essentially instantaneous.

questions.q: Mass defect is defined as the:
options: difference between the mass of the constituent nucleons and the nucleus
questions.explain: Mass defect is the difference between the total mass of separate nucleons and the assembled nucleus.

questions.q: In an electron diffraction tube, increasing the accelerating voltage causes the diffraction rings to:
questions.explain: Higher voltage gives electrons greater momentum and shorter de Broglie wavelength, so the diffraction rings shrink.

questions.q: The nucleus with the highest binding energy per nucleon is around:
questions.explain: Iron-56 sits near the peak of the binding-energy-per-nucleon curve, the most stable region.

questions.q: The work function of a metal is the:
options: Minimum energy needed to release an electron from the metal surface
Kinetic energy of the fastest electron
questions.explain: The work function φ is the minimum energy required to liberate an electron from the metal's surface.

questions.q: A graph of maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons against frequency has a gradient equal to:
questions.explain: From KEmax = hf − φ, the gradient of KEmax against f is the Planck constant h.

questions.q: In a photoelectric experiment, the stopping potential V_s relates to maximum KE by:
questions.explain: The stopping potential just halts the fastest electrons, so eV_s = ½mv²max, the maximum kinetic energy.

questions.q: Gamma radiation differs from alpha and beta in that it:
questions.explain: Gamma radiation is a high-energy photon (electromagnetic wave) with no mass or charge.

questions.q: Nuclear fission of a large nucleus releases energy because the products have:
questions.explain: The fragments lie nearer the peak of the curve with higher binding energy per nucleon, releasing energy.

questions.q: Fusion in stars requires very high temperatures mainly to:
options: overcome the electrostatic repulsion between nuclei
questions.explain: High kinetic energy lets positively charged nuclei approach closely despite Coulomb repulsion.

questions.q: On the N-Z stability graph, light stable nuclei lie:
options: close to the N = Z line
questions.explain: Light stable nuclei lie near N = Z; heavier ones need more neutrons (curve above the line).

questions.q: A sample has a half-life of 8 days. What fraction remains after 24 days?
questions.explain: 24 days is three half-lives, so (1/2)^3 = 1/8 of the sample remains.

questions.q: Einstein's photoelectric equation is best written as:
questions.explain: hf = φ + ½mv²max: photon energy equals the work function plus the maximum kinetic energy of the electron.

questions.q: A nucleus above the stability line (neutron-rich) typically decays by:
questions.explain: Neutron-rich nuclei undergo beta-minus decay, converting a neutron to a proton.

questions.q: A line emission spectrum consists of discrete coloured lines because:
options: Atomic electrons occupy only discrete energy levels
questions.explain: Discrete spectral lines arise because electrons occupy quantised energy levels, so only specific photon energies are emitted.

questions.q: When an electron in an atom moves from a higher to a lower energy level, the atom:
options: Emits a photon of energy equal to the difference between the levels
questions.explain: The electron emits a photon whose energy equals the difference between the two energy levels, hf = E₁ − E₂.

questions.q: The de Broglie hypothesis applies to:
options: All moving particles, though the effect is significant only for very small masses
questions.explain: All moving matter has a de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p, but it is only measurable for tiny masses like electrons.

questions.q: Which is a typical product set of uranium-235 induced fission?
options: Two equal helium nuclei and no neutrons
Two lighter daughter nuclei plus two or three neutrons
questions.explain: U-235 fission produces two unequal daughter nuclei plus 2-3 neutrons and energy.

questions.q: A mass defect of 1.0 u corresponds to a binding energy of approximately:
questions.explain: One atomic mass unit is equivalent to about 931.5 MeV of energy.

questions.q: A chain reaction is sustained when each fission event causes on average:
questions.explain: A self-sustaining chain reaction requires at least one neutron per fission to trigger another.

questions.q: Which graph correctly describes how the activity of a sample changes with time?
questions.explain: Activity A = lambda N decreases exponentially because N decreases exponentially.

questions.q: An electron drops from an energy level of −1.5 eV to −3.4 eV. The energy of the emitted photon is:
questions.explain: Photon energy = |E_final − E_initial| = |−3.4 − (−1.5)| = 1.9 eV.

questions.q: The y-intercept of a maximum-KE-versus-frequency graph for the photoelectric effect equals:
questions.explain: From KEmax = hf − φ, the intercept on the KE axis is −φ (negative of the work function).

questions.q: Nuclear fusion of small nuclei releases energy because the product nucleus has:
questions.explain: Fusing light nuclei moves up the steep left side of the curve, increasing binding energy per nucleon.

questions.q: Experiments show nuclear radius R relates to nucleon number A by:
questions.explain: Nuclear radius scales as R = r0 A^(1/3), where r0 is about 1.2 fm.

questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle is given by:
questions.explain: The de Broglie wavelength is λ = h/p, where p is the particle's momentum.

questions.q: Binding energy is the energy:
options: required to separate a nucleus into its individual nucleons
questions.explain: Binding energy equals the work needed to completely separate a nucleus into free nucleons.

questions.q: How many photons of wavelength 600 nm are needed to deliver 1.0 J of energy? (E ≈ 3.3 × 10⁻¹⁹ J per photon)
questions.explain: Number = total energy / photon energy = 1.0 / 3.3×10⁻¹⁹ ≈ 3.0×10¹⁸ photons.
